For **a full day or longer**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity and a **2,600 W** output; the cited estimate is about a day for a 100 W ceramic heat emitter controlled by a thermostat. The actual runtime depends on how often the heater runs and the station’s conversion losses. ([capacity and runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

For a smaller, shorter backup, the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh) is estimated to run a 24 W heat mat for about **6–8 hours**. A larger alternative, the **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh), is estimated at **15–18 hours** for a 100 W emitter on a thermostat. ([comparison](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

Before buying, check your heater’s wattage and size for the outage duration you need. Keep the **thermostat in the circuit**, and insulate the enclosure to help conserve heat; Petco also recommends having emergency heat sources ready. ([reptile outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
